profiles.name: Aftanasy Litvakoff
profiles.query: "Aftanasy Litvakoff" Red Scare deportation 1921 portrait photograph
profiles.identity_context:
Aftanasy Litvakoff was born about 1884 in Lopatni, Chernihiv, Russia (present-day Ukraine). Immigrated to the United States in 1913.

Lived in Homestead, Pennsylvania for six years and joined the URW there in 1917. Arrested for distributing radical handbills, he served twenty days in jail. After moving to Cleveland he was arrested again February 21, 1921. He stated, “I do recognize Anarchism, but I feel that I am not worthy enough to be called such, owing to the fat that I do not understand Anarchy enough to be honored by being called an Anarchist.” Deported to Russia March 18, 1921.

Adapted from Kenyon Zimmer, Red Scare Deportees (kenyonzimmer.com), compiled from INS deportation case files.

profiles.name: Mikhail Bilokumsky
profiles.query: "Mikhail Bilokumsky" Red Scare deportation 1921 portrait photograph
profiles.identity_context:
Mikhail Bilokumsky was born 1892 in Andreevka, Russia (present-day Ukraine). Worked as a laborer. Immigrated to the United States in 1912.

Member of the United Communist Party (the result of a merger between the Communist Labor Party and part of the Communist Party of America in 1920). Arrested in Philadelphia in January 1921 during the second Palmer Raids, and again in April 1921 while distributing UCP May Day leaflets. Ordered deported to Russia in August 1921 on the basis of the revolutionary content of those handbills. His legal challenge failed before the U.S. Supreme Court in United States ex rel. Bilokumsky v. Tod (1923). Because the Soviet Union no longer accepted deportees from the United States, officials attempted to use a passport issued by the unrecognized “Ukrainian Diplomatic Mission,” but this document was invalid. Although an Immigration Bureau board recommended his release in January 1924 due to the impossibility of lawful deportation, officials nevertheless deported him May 24, 1924.

Routed through Switzerland to the Russian border, he was refused entry. Last reported to be stranded and starving in Vienna.

Adapted from Kenyon Zimmer, Red Scare Deportees (kenyonzimmer.com), compiled from INS deportation case files.

profiles.name: Walter Nichiperuck
profiles.query: "Walter Nichiperuck" Red Scare deportation 1921 portrait photograph
profiles.identity_context:
Walter Nichiperuck was born in 1894 in Grodno in the Russian Empire, in what is now principally Belarus, and served as secretary of a Hartford, Connecticut branch of the Union of Russian Workers.

He was administratively deported to Russia on January 22, 1921. THIS WAS ADMINISTRATIVE IMMIGRATION DETENTION AND DEPORTATION, NOT A CRIMINAL CONVICTION, and the record is classified accordingly.

Hartford saw substantial Palmer-era raids in which many Russian workers were detained, but GROUP DETENTION DATES MUST NOT BE ASSIGNED TO HIM without his individual immigration file, and none are. The underlying individual file was not retrievable, so these details rest on the supplied transcription of the Zimmer project record, which was built from federal immigration files.

His name in the original language, alternative transliterations, exact birth date and place, arrest and detention dates, detention facility, deportation vessel and port, later life and death are all unresolved.

profiles.name: Walter Sherwen
profiles.query: "Walter Sherwen" Red Scare deportation 1921 portrait photograph
profiles.identity_context: Walter Sherwen, also recorded as Wherwan and Wladylaw Czerwonajcio, was a Polish carpenter born in 1892 near Suwałki in the Russian Empire. He immigrated to the United States in 1913 and joined Polish Branch No. 37 of the Communist Party in Detroit. The federal government deported him to Russia on February 26, 1921.
